comparison: Both evaluations address C53 regarding the broad requirement of Lsd1 across somatic cell types. OpenEval finds this claim extends beyond the hematopoietic data presented and represents speculative generalization. Peer reviewers similarly express uncertainty, explicitly asking whether Lsd1 is broadly required or preferentially required for certain cell types, indicating the generalizability claim needs additional discussion or evidence.

Both evaluations address C56 regarding therapeutic implications of Lsd1 inhibition on hematopoiesis. OpenEval finds this a reasonable inference from the severe hematopoietic defects observed. Peer reviewers accept this finding and request discussion of therapeutic implications, acknowledging that Lsd1 inhibition would be problematic for hematopoiesis.

Both address claims about localized vs. global H3K4 methylation changes (C36-C39, C43, C49, C75). OpenEval supports these claims based on Western blot and ChIP-Seq data showing no global changes but localized increases. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, specifically asking whether global H3K4me2/me1 changes correlate with Lsd1 reduction and requesting discussion of alternative Lsd1-mediated mechanisms, suggesting the H3K4 methylation mechanism alone may not fully explain phenotypes.

Both address claims about Lsd1 target enrichment and dual enhancer-promoter regulation (C40, C41, C52, C74). OpenEval supports these based on enrichment analysis with significant p-values and identification of biologically relevant targets. Peer reviewers find this conceptually interesting and describe it as a strength, accepting the dual regulation mechanism.

Both address gene expression claims showing upregulation of HSPC signatures (C28-C31, C47, C70, C72-C73). OpenEval supports these based on GSEA analysis with appropriate statistical methods and validation. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this observation as conceptually interesting and praise the integration of ChIP-seq with gene expression profiling.

Both address hematopoietic defect claims (C14-C18, plus peer includes C2, C44-C46). OpenEval supports these based on converging evidence from multiple measurements with appropriate quantification. Peer reviewers state the manuscript is technically well done and acknowledge it shows HSCs and hematopoiesis depend on Lsd1, though they note the requirement was previously shown by Sprussel et al.

Both address ChIP-Seq and enhancer binding claims (C32-C34, C42, C4, C50-C51). OpenEval supports these based on ChIP-Seq data with validation showing >85% concordance. Peer reviewers challenge the novelty claim, noting multiple studies have shown LSD1 functions through enhancers, and question presenting this as novel discovery. While not rejecting the data itself, they express uncertainty about its presentation.

Both address lineage-specific maturation defects (C24-C27, plus peer includes C20-C23). OpenEval supports these based on flow cytometry and phenotypic analysis with appropriate Cre drivers. Peer reviewers note the manuscript is technically well done but raise specific concerns about HSC quantification, stating effects are not apparent when gating on definitive markers in Figure 2, and request additional data to clarify HSC frequency.

Both address Lsd1 binding patterns and enhancer regulation (C4-C5, C50-C51). OpenEval supports these based on ChIP-Seq showing binding patterns and H3K4me1 changes at enhancers. Peer reviewers challenge the novelty, citing existing literature on LSD1 functions through enhancers, questioning statements that suggest this is a new finding.

Both address the causal link between gene derepression and differentiation defects (C2-C3, C6, C44, C48, C52, C71, C73). OpenEval supports the main conclusions based on comprehensive integration of phenotypic, gene expression, and epigenomic data. Peer reviewers accept the general finding but request additional mechanistic information about cell death or proliferation changes, suggesting they want more detail to fully support the causal link.

Both address functional differentiation defects (C19-C21 for OpenEval; C20-C21 overlap with peer). OpenEval supports these based on complementary approaches including single-cell qPCR and colony assays. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about HSC quantification and the magnitude of effects claimed, requesting additional bar graphs to clarify HSC frequency.

Both address competitive transplantation and self-renewal defects (C22-C23, C46). OpenEval supports these based on loss of donor chimerism and HSC/progenitor populations. Peer reviewers acknowledge the manuscript is technically well done and accept that Lsd1 is required for HSC function, though they note this was previously shown.

OpenEval addresses background/literature claims (C1, C7-C13, C54-C55, C57-C69) representing established knowledge with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims, as peer reviewers focused on novel findings rather than cited literature.
